impact:
Byte-parity divergence in the frozen `could not parse ccusage output.` diagnostic, and a possible U+FFFD on the wire.

`src/ccusage.ts:49` does `res.stderr.slice(0, 400)`; `usage.py:124` does `out.stderr[:400]`. Python slices CODE POINTS, JS slices UTF-16 CODE UNITS, so any astral character in ccusage's stderr desynchronises them. Measured:

  python3 -c "s='😀'*300+'TAIL'; print(len(s[:400]), s[:400].endswith('TAIL'))"
  -> 304 True
  node -e "const s='😀'.repeat(300)+'TAIL'; const c=s.slice(0,400); console.log(c.length, [...c].length, c.endsWith('TAIL'))"
  -> 400 200 false        # the informative tail is dropped

Worse, slicing at an odd offset can cut a surrogate pair in half:
  node -e "const c='😀'.repeat(300).slice(0,401); console.log(Buffer.from(c,'utf8').subarray(-4).toString('hex'))"
  -> 80efbfbd             # trailing U+FFFD

This is NOT in tests/golden/ALLOWLIST.md, so it is an unsanctioned divergence in a message the allowlist treats as frozen.

Pre-existing (introduced with the T-003 port of run_ccusage), NOT introduced by T-006, and outside T-006's changed files — filed rather than fixed inline per the ticket's scope rule. It is the same hazard class T-006 fixed one layer down in `truncateUtf8` (byte-based, boundary-safe), so the fix is to give this site the same treatment: slice by code point (`[...s].slice(0, 400).join("")`) to match Python exactly, or reuse a boundary-safe helper.

Found by code review round 4 (differential harness over usage.py).
title: stderr truncation in ccusage.ts slices UTF-16 units where Python slices code points
